Introduction

What Is a Public Limited Company?

A Public Limited Company is registered under the Companies Act, 2013, with the ability to offer its shares to the public and, if listed, trade them on a stock exchange. It carries more shareholders, more directors, and a significantly higher compliance framework than a Private Limited Company.

This structure suits businesses with a genuine plan to raise capital broadly or eventually pursue a public listing — the governance overhead is substantial and worth weighing carefully against a Private Limited Company first.

Advantages & Disadvantages

Advantages

  • Ability to raise capital from the public, including via a stock exchange listing
  • Limited liability protection for all shareholders
  • High credibility with large investors, lenders and institutions
  • Shares are freely transferable, unlike a Private Limited Company

Disadvantages

  • Substantially higher compliance burden, including SEBI regulations if listed
  • Requires a minimum of 7 shareholders and 3 directors
  • Higher cost of incorporation and ongoing governance
  • Greater public disclosure requirements

Eligibility

Who Can Register a Public Limited Company

  • Minimum 7 shareholders, with no upper limit
  • Minimum 3 directors, at least one resident in India
  • No minimum capital requirement under current rules
  • A registered office address in India
  • Directors must have a valid DIN and DSC

Step-by-Step

Registration Process & Timeline

1. DSC & Name Reservation

Obtain DSC for directors and reserve the company name via the RUN/SPICe+ service.

2. Drafting MOA & AOA

We draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association reflecting the company's objects and governance rules.

3. SPICe+ Filing with ROC

Incorporation application filed with the Registrar of Companies along with PAN & TAN application.

4. Certificate of Incorporation

Once approved, you receive the Certificate of Incorporation. Timelines can vary and typically run longer than a Private Limited Company given the additional scrutiny.

Required Documents

What You'll Need

  • PAN card of all directors & shareholders
  • Aadhaar / address proof of all directors
  • Passport-size photographs
  • Proof of registered office (utility bill + NOC from owner)

Annual Compliance

Ongoing Requirements After Registration

  • Annual ROC filing (AOC-4 & MGT-7)
  • Statutory audit of financial statements
  • Additional SEBI compliance if the company is listed
  • Regular board and shareholder meetings as prescribed
  • Director KYC (DIR-3 KYC) for all directors
